title: The Magic Garden Game
text: Imagine playing a game in a huge garden. Someone becomes the 'Plant Fairy'. The Plant Fairy points and says, 'Touch a tree with a thick trunk!' or 'Bring me a leaf with a jagged edge!' Would you know where to run to find them?

title: A Garden Mystery
text: Have you ever stopped to look closely at the plants around you? Why do some plants grow tall like giants, while others creep along the ground? Why are some leaves huge and round, while others are tiny and sharp like needles?

content.title: Exploring Different Leaves
content.description: Look at these different shapes. Some are round, some are long, some have smooth edges, and some look like a saw! They even come in different colors like green, yellow, red, or purple.

title: The Parts of a Plant
text: Plants have different parts that make them unique. The thick, hard woody stem of a big tree is called the Trunk. The flat, green part that makes food for the plant is the Leaf. The edge of the leaf is called its Margin.

content.question: If the Plant Fairy asked you to touch a plant with a thin, green stem, which one would you touch?

title: Your Favorite Leaf
text: Close your eyes and think of a leaf you recently saw. Was it smooth or rough? Did it have a special smell, like mint or coriander? Explain how it felt to someone sitting next to you.

title: Nature's Designs
text: In ancient Indian texts, different leaves are used for different purposes. The large, round Lotus leaf is used to serve food because water doesn't stick to it! Just like we wear different clothes, plants grow leaves suited for where they live.

content.tip: Encourage students to smell different leaves like mint, lemon, or neem. This engages multiple senses and helps them remember the unique characteristics of each plant.

content.mistake: Thinking all leaves are green. Leaves can be red, yellow, or even purple! The color depends on the specific pigments inside the leaf.

content.title: Leaf and Trunk Rubbing
content.description: Place a paper over a leaf with thick veins or against the rough bark of a tree trunk. Gently rub a crayon over the paper to create a beautiful natural print! Compare the patterns you find.
